message.content:
I’m sorry—I don’t have real‑time market feeds available right now, so I can’t give you the exact spot price at this moment.  

If you need the most recent figure, here’s what you can do:

| Source | How to get it |
|--------|---------------|
| **CoinMarketCap** | Visit <https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/bitcoin/> – the “Price” field shows USD, BTC, ETH, etc., updated every few seconds. |
| **Binance / Coinbase Pro** | Use their public APIs (`GET https://api.binance.com/api/v3/ticker/price?symbol=BTCUSDT` or `GET https://api.pro.coinbase.com/products/BTC-USDC/stats`). |
| **CryptoCompare** | Endpoint `<https://min-api.cryptocompare.com/data/pricemultifull>` returns multi‑currency quotes. |
| **Google Finance** | Search “Bitcoin price” or visit <https://www.google.com/search?q=btc+usd> – Google pulls the latest ticker. |

Feel free to let me know which platform you prefer, and I can walk through the steps or show sample code snippets!
message.reasoning:
User asks about current Bitcoin price. We can use an API or external data source; but we have no direct internet access. However maybe there's a tool to fetch real-time data? No such tool defined. So likely answer with placeholder or explanation that cannot retrieve live data.

We could say we don't have up-to-date info. Or ask user if they'd like approximate value as of last known update (like using some dataset). But better respond that I can't provide real-time prices due to lack of connectivity. Provide guidance on how to check via websites etc.

Thus produce response accordingly.
